summary: jailfs is a stdlib-only Python package giving each agent session one writable directory and a list of read-only roots, enforced by the kernel through per-root directory descriptors and component-by-component openat walks with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY, plus an exclusively created random temporary file renamed into place. Reads search the writable root then the read roots in order, saves go only to the writable root and are refused for links, directories, shadows of read-root names, duplicates within one batch() block, and replacement of a file the session read (compared by device+inode, with the written exemption). Every refusal is a Refused with a code from E_ACCESS/E_NOT_FOUND/E_DUPLICATE/E_SHADOW and a fix naming the roots, and 119 tests plus a 14-mutation harness confirm each hole is actually pinned.

pattern_mapping.Start-up check: jailfs/workspace.py Workspace.__init__ (list/tuple root refused with a --read fix, root must exist and be a directory, duplicate read roots collapsed by real path) and Workspace._refuse_overlaps (same directory, read inside writable, writable inside read)
pattern_mapping.Writable and read roots: jailfs/workspace.py Workspace._root/_reads plus Location(root, parts, writable); the writable root is always roots[0]
pattern_mapping.Locator: jailfs/workspace.py Workspace._locate and jailfs/paths.py (split_relative folds . and .. lexically and refuses a climb; within compares an absolute path lexically against each root's given and real spelling; the agent's path is never resolved)
pattern_mapping.Root handle: jailfs/handle.py RootHandle (one O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW descriptor per resolved root; _parent walks components with os.open(..., dir_fd=), lstat/exists/read_file/walk_files all go through it)
pattern_mapping.Writer: jailfs/handle.py RootHandle.write_file and _create_temp (random .jailfs-tmp-<hex> name created with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW in the target's directory, fsync, os.replace with src_dir_fd/dst_dir_fd, temp unlinked on failure, identity taken after the rename)
pattern_mapping.Shadow check: jailfs/workspace.py Workspace.save, the loop over self._reads calling handle.exists(loc.parts) — checked on the canonical relative name however the path was spelled
pattern_mapping.Opened set: jailfs/workspace.py Workspace._opened/_written (identity = (st_dev, st_ino) from handle.identity; added by read/load, written added after the rename; save refuses only when identity in opened and not in written)
pattern_mapping.Loader: jailfs/workspace.py Workspace.load — .py/.js only, resolved through the locator like a read, decoded as UTF-8; jailfs/__init__.py exports no open/eval/compile/import_module/require, so there is no other way in

notes_applied: Note 1 (let the OS enforce the root): no os.Root in the stdlib, so every path is walked one component at a time from the root's directory fd with os.open(..., O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY, dir_fd=) and the last component is lstat'ed; ELOOP/ENOTDIR map to E_ACCESS. Every link below a root is refused, the stricter option the note allows.

Note 2 (resolve roots once, never the agent's path): RootHandle resolves given via abspath then realpath at start-up; _locate matches absolute paths with os.path.normpath against both spellings and never calls realpath on them — a mutation that swaps normpath for realpath is caught by test_save_absolute_path_of_in_root_link_refused.

Note 3 (keep roots disjoint): _refuse_overlaps refuses a read root inside the writable root, the writable root inside a read root, and the same directory twice, all on resolved paths (so a symlinked alias is caught).

Note 4 (exclusive random temp, then rename): write_file creates .jailfs-tmp-<12 bytes hex> with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, retries on EEXIST, unlinks on any failure, and os.replace's it over the target, so a planted temp symlink fails instead of being followed and a hard link to an input never carries the write.

Note 5 (identities not names): opened/written sets compare (st_dev, st_ino); the written exemption lets a session re-save its own output; hard-linked files are not refused for being linked, and the check is against the target's lstat identity, not its name.
Note 6 (a save can shadow a read-only file): save refuses E_SHADOW when the canonical relative name exists in any read root, checked for relative and absolute spellings alike.
Note 7 (one way to load code): load() is the only loader and goes through the locator; the package exports nothing that can load a file another way, and a test asserts no such name is public.
Note 8 (strict flags): a list/tuple/set root is refused at construction with a fix pointing at --read instead of silently taking the last value; a mutation making it last-value-wins is caught.

Note 9 (resolve and show names the same way): read, save and load all coerce str/bytes/os.PathLike through paths.as_text and share the same locator; refusals name the roots, and E_NOT_FOUND lists up to eight names from the writable root.

Note 10 (one workspace per run, ordered refusals): batch() marks one agent program's run and E_DUPLICATE fires on the same canonical path twice; save reports in the chapter's fixed order shape, access, duplicate, shadow, replacing-an-opened-file; nested batches share the union and pop in a finally.

Note 11 (require each regression test to fail without its fix): tests/mutation_check.py copies the package, deletes one fix at a time (14 mutations, including missing O_NOFOLLOW, non-exclusive temp, deleted link/directory/shadow/opened/overlap/duplicate checks, realpath on agent paths) and requires the named test to go red after verifying it is green unmutated; two vacuous tests were found this way and strengthened.
tests: 119 tests in 8 unittest modules under tests/ (startup, read, save, identity, batch, names/load, refusals, atomic), plus tests/mutation_check.py with 14 mutations; last run: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → Ran 119 tests in 0.116s, OK; `python3 tests/mutation_check.py` → all 14 mutations were caught by their own test.
chapter_feedback: The Structure table and the plain-text sketch translated almost line for line, which made the design phase fast; the explicit note that Python has no os.Root (note 1) saved me from writing a string-checking fallback.

Note 11 was the most valuable part: it caught two of my own tests passing without their fix ('some refusal happened' instead of 'the link refusal happened', and a fix text that contained --read by accident). Without it I would have shipped both.

The chapter gives only three refusal kinds (access, shape, shadow) while TASK.md fixes four codes and no shape code, so 'save onto a directory' had to become E_ACCESS with a fix naming a file inside — a guess the chapter could have settled in one sentence.

The refusal order in note 10 is stated as a list but not tied to concrete cases; I had to work out by experiment that a target that is a directory in a read root (but absent from the writable root) is E_SHADOW, not a shape refusal, and that duplicate beats shadow.

The chapter says roots may be spelled two ways (given and resolved) but does not mention that on macOS /var is itself a link, so a path spelled through one alias of the temp directory matched neither spelling; I fixed my fixture, but a note about matching more than two spellings (or about test fixtures) would help.

Note 5's 'do not refuse hard-linked files' is ambiguous: it reads as sage advice at first glance but actually means 'do not refuse a save merely because the target has other links; rely on rename', which I only settled after writing the hard-link tests.

Nothing in the chapter says whether names() should be recursive or files-only, and the chapter's smallest-form variation would have dropped the opened set and shadow check entirely — the task's E_SHADOW and 'would replace a file this session read' codes are what decided both, so the chapter and the task pull slightly in different directions.
